study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier given in the paper.

subject_id.notes: Per-subject IDs not provided in main text; may exist in Supplementary Table 1 which is not included.

sample_id.notes: No sample-level identifiers reported in provided text.

pmid.notes: PubMed ID not stated within the paper text itself.

subcohort.notes: The paper defines comparison groups (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US) but does not use the term 'subcohort'.

target_condition.notes: This is a lifestyle/microbiome comparative study, not a disease-condition study; no specific disease phenotype is reported.

control.notes: No explicit case/control framework; groups compared are lifestyle categories (traditional vs urban), not disease cases/controls.

country.evidence_quote: the Matses from the Peruvian Amazon ( n = 24)
country.section: Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity of the Gut Microbiomes
country.notes: Matses country derived from 'Peruvian Amazon'. Tunapuco country not explicitly stated (only 'Andean highlands' given).

body_site.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample
body_site.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
body_site.notes: Applies uniformly to all groups compared (gut/fecal metagenomics).

days_from_first_collection.notes: Study appears to be single time-point sampling; no longitudinal data reported.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: The Yanomami group is mainly hunter–gatherers
lifestyle.section: Results — Lifestyle of the Human Group Studied
lifestyle.notes: Matses/Yanomami-Venezuela quote: 'two hunter–gatherer communities [Yanomami from Venezuela, n = 8...Matses, n = 24]'; Tunapuco quote: 'a rural agricultural community [Tunapuco, n = 12]' (Methods — Bioinformatics Processing). US group not assigned a traditional lifestyle category (urban-industrialized).

location.evidence_quote: the Matses from the Peruvian Amazon ( n = 24) ( Obregon-Tito et al., 2015 ), the Tunapuco from the Andean highlands ( n = 12)
location.section: Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity of the Gut Microbiomes

westernized.notes: Traditional groups explicitly contrasted with 'urban-industrialized' group; westernized status inferred from lifestyle classification rather than literal Yes/No statement.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Total DNA was extracted from 15 stool samples with FastDNA ® SPIN Kit (MP Biomedicals)
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
dna_extraction_kit.notes: DNA extraction kit only reported for newly generated Yanomami/Brazil samples; other datasets are reanalyzed published data with no kit description here.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208
ncbi_accession.notes: This accession pertains only to newly generated Yanomami/Brazil data; other groups' data are from previously published BioProjects not specified in this text.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq ® 2500 sequencer (Oswaldo Cruz Foundation, high-throughput sequencing platform)
sequencing_platform.section: Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
sequencing_platform.notes: Other datasets' platform reported only generically: 'These datasets were sequenced on Illumina platforms' (Methods — Bioinformatics Processing), lacking model specificity required for the enum.

age.evidence_quote: At the time of the collection, age and gender information of the individuals were also acquired.
age.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
age.notes: Actual age values deferred to Supplementary Table 1, not included in provided text.

ancestry.notes: Ethnic group names (Yanomami, Matses, Tunapuco) are given but no formal ancestry category term is used.

sex.evidence_quote: Association between gut microbiome composition and gender was analyzed with principal coordinate analysis
sex.section: Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity of the Gut Microbiomes
sex.notes: Gender/sex was analyzed as a variable but individual-level sex values or counts are not reported in the main text.

age_min.notes: Age data mentioned as collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, not in provided text.

age_max.notes: Age data mentioned as collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, not in provided text.

age_years.notes: At the time of the collection, age and gender information of the individuals were also acquired, but values summarized in Supplementary Table 1 not included in provided text.

dietary_restriction.notes: Diet described qualitatively (fruits, fiber, sylvatic animals, hunting/gathering) but not as a formal dietary restriction category.

disease.notes: Paper states chronic diseases like atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami, but no explicit per-participant disease status is reported.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: there is a contrasting higher abundance of Escherichia and Ralstonia genera in the Yanomami/Brazil, and therefore, they were defined as Yanomami/Brazil biomarkers
biomarker_name.notes: Additional biomarkers (Neisseria, Desulfovibrio, Klebsiella, Cutibacterium, Akkermansia, Treponema, Brachyspira, Roseburia, Anaerostipes, Eubacterium, Flavonifactor, Enterococcus, Streptococcus) also identified as group-specific biomarkers via LEfSe/LDA across Results and Discussion sections.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: LDA score of >4.0 were used as thresholds
biomarker_unit.notes: LDA score is the statistical threshold used for biomarker detection (LEfSe), but individual biomarker LDA score values are not reported in text (only shown in Figure 3C, not extractable as verbatim text values).

biomarker_value.notes: Specific LDA score values per biomarker are shown only in Figure 3C (bar chart), not given as text values.

disease_response_os.notes: Study is a microbiome characterization study; overall survival not applicable/reported.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable to this study design.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not applicable; no clinical performance status assessed in this gut microbiome study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal samples collected but no standardized 'feces_phenotype' scale (e.g., Bristol stool score) reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

value: Yanomami is the largest semi-nomadic hunter-gatherer group of the Americas

uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208
uncurated_metadata.notes: Miscellaneous descriptive/lifestyle and data-repository metadata not captured by structured fields.

host_species.evidence_quote: Human groups that still maintain traditional modes of subsistence (hunter–gatherers and rural agriculturalists) represent human groups non-impacted by urban-industrialized lifestyles
host_species.notes: Species not stated as 'Homo sapiens' verbatim but clearly refers to human participants (Yanomami, Matses, Tunapuco, US individuals) throughout the paper.
